name: Data Storage Converter
description: Convert file and storage sizes between bits, bytes, and both decimal (KB/MB/GB/TB) and binary (KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB) units — correctly, without conflating the two.

faq.question: Why does my "1 TB" drive show up as ~931 GB in my operating system?
faq.answer: The drive is advertised using decimal terabytes (1 TB = 1,000,000,000,000 bytes), while most operating systems report free space in binary units — 931 GiB (which they often mislabel "GB") — because 1 TB of decimal bytes is only about 0.909 TiB. Nothing is missing; it's the same number of bytes described two different ways.

faq.question: Which should I use — decimal or binary?
faq.answer: Use decimal (KB/MB/GB/TB) when matching a manufacturer's advertised capacity or network transfer rate. Use binary (KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB) when matching what your operating system or RAM specifications report, since memory has always been addressed in power-of-two units.
